data.about: The same 6 m span as task 1a and the same 120 kN in total — but spread out as 20 kN/m instead of dropped at one point. Spread out, the cable answers with a parabola rather than a kink. Task 1c then asks the question worth asking: is the force the same all along it? Drag the extra tangent and read the answer off the force plan — every ray is a tangent, and the outermost ones are the longest.

steps.caption: UE 3 task 1b: the same span and the same total load as task 1a, but spread evenly along the cable. Design a form for it and draw the force plan
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: left: the supports A and B, and a uniform load q_d over the whole 6 m. Nothing yet says how deep the cable hangs
steps.title: What is given

steps.caption: left: a uniform load has a resultant of q·L acting through the middle — and it is the same 120 kN that task 1a dropped at a single point. The dashed line through A and B is the closing string CS/SL
steps.title: First the resultant

steps.caption: left: with the load spread out the cable answers with a parabola, not a kink. Its end tangents 1 and 2 meet at I below midspan — right: those two tangents are the outer rays, and they cross at the pole
steps.title: Now design: choose the sag

steps.caption: again the pole’s distance from the load line — and again it is constant along the whole cable, crown to support
steps.title: The horizontal thrust

steps.caption: the reactions pull along the end tangents — the flattest the cable ever is at its ends, so this is where it pulls hardest
steps.title: Global equilibrium

steps.caption: the sheet asks it directly. Subdivide the load line and draw a ray for every strip: each ray is the tangent at one point of the cable, and their lengths are visibly different. So no — the force changes all along it
steps.title: c) Is the force constant?

steps.caption: left: a tangent at any point you like — right: its ray. Drag it along the cable: as it swings toward a support the ray gets longer, toward the crown it gets shorter and flatter
steps.title: c) Draw one more tangent

steps.caption: the horizontal part never changes, so the force is decided entirely by the vertical part — which is zero at the crown and largest at the supports. The longest rays are the outermost ones
steps.title: c) The answer

data.title: EX 3.1b — a cable under a line load, and where it works hardest
